title: Pain and Skin Innervation in Patients with Fabry Disease
summary:
Fabry disease is a rare inherited disorder in which certain substances accumulate in different organs and tissues of the body. Many people with Fabry disease experience burning pain, especially in their hands and feet. The causes of this pain are not yet fully understood, and currently available treatments are not effective for all patients.

The aim of this study is to improve our understanding of changes in the small nerve fibers in the skin and how these changes are related to pain. The study will also investigate how currently available treatment options affect pain and nerve function.

Adult patients with Fabry disease who receive care at the Fabry Center of the University Hospital Würzburg will participate. During their routine follow-up visits, participants will complete pain questionnaires and undergo examinations to assess nerve function. In addition, blood samples and a small skin sample will be collected. Patients who, as part of their routine medical care, choose treatment with a pain-relieving skin patch or a dietary supplement will be followed for three months to assess changes in pain and nerve function.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
For participation in the therapeutic observational part of the study, patients must report a pain intensity of ≥4, both verbally and in the Würzburg Fabry Pain Questionnaire, either at the time of assessment or during the previous 4 weeks. This level of pain must be present for more than 10% of the time, or patients must report a subjective need for analgesic treatment. In addition, during a routine clinical visit, patients must have chosen treatment with either a topical capsaicin patch (Qutenza®) or palmitoylethanolamide (PEA) from the available analgesic treatment options offered according to the current guideline for neuropathic pain and the current evidence. 
All participants must be at least 18 years of age at the time of study enrollment.
Exclusion criteria:
Insufficient proficiency in the German language or inability to provide informed consent independently.
For the treatment part: absence of pain, no subjective burden caused by pain, or contraindication to either treatment.
For the skin biopsy: anticoagulant therapy or other coagulation disorders, pronounced ankle edema, or inflammatory or trophic skin changes at the biopsy site.
